solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Good to board a bright Venetian vessel (6)

indicatorNotes.to board: G boards ROSY the way a passenger boards a ship, getting inside it

blocks.note: rosy = bright, as in a rosy future

annotation.surface: A cheerful gondolier steps aboard a gleaming boat in Venice.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Good to board' reads as fit to get on the boat; it is an instruction to put G inside, just after the first letter.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym with a historical flavour: an argosy is a large merchant ship, of the kind Venice sent out in The Merchant of Venice.

entries.clue: Desert area with river coursing through central Qatar (7)

indicatorNotes.coursing through: a river courses through land, so the river's letters run through the others
indicatorNotes.central: takes the middle letters of Qatar

blocks.note: the middle three letters of qATAr
the Cam, the river through Cambridge

annotation.surface: A travel note about a dry region of the Gulf with a river flowing across it.
annotation.walkthrough: Qatar is a desert country, which pulls you toward the Gulf; the answer is in South America, and Qatar is only there for its middle.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the Atacama in northern Chile is one of the driest deserts on Earth.

entries.clue: Lord Chancellor keeps this rat eagles tormented (5,4)

indicatorNotes.tormented: tormented letters are twisted out of shape

annotation.surface: A cruel Lord Chancellor keeps a rat and some eagles to torture.
annotation.walkthrough: The Lord Chancellor is formally Keeper of the Great Seal, the seal used on state documents, so the definition is a description rather than a synonym.
annotation.definitionFit: A descriptive definition: in Britain the Lord Chancellor's old title includes keeper of the Great Seal of the Realm.

entries.clue: 16 9 church in Leicester — in Leicester — regularly given ground (6,12,7)

indicatorNotes.regularly: takes every other letter of given, at regular intervals
indicatorNotes.ground: ground letters are broken up and remade, like grain in a mill

blocks.note: CE (Church of England) placed inside LEICESTER

annotation.surface: A church in Leicester has had its land handed over, with the town named twice for emphasis.
annotation.walkthrough: 16 and 9 are ESPIONAGE and AGENCY, so the definition is 'espionage agency'. The repeated 'in Leicester' is not a stammer: the first is the container, the second is fodder. Leicester is an English city.
annotation.definitionFit: The Secret Intelligence Service, better known as MI6, is Britain's foreign espionage agency.

entries.clue: Shipped in from island refuge surrounded by sea (8)

indicatorNotes.surrounded by: the refuge is ringed by the sea, as an island harbour is, so the sea's letters go round it

blocks.note: a port is a refuge, as in any port in a storm

annotation.surface: Goods arrive from an island harbour ringed by ocean.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole surface is shipping talk, so it is easy to miss that the definition is the first two words only.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: goods brought into a country by ship or otherwise from abroad.

entries.clue: Old woman trained female thick-knee for Messer (4,3,5)

indicatorNotes.trained: trained means shaped into a new form

annotation.surface: An old woman trains a female thick-knee, a wading bird, on behalf of someone called Messer.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Messer' looks like a surname or a clumsy person; it is the German name of the Threepenny Opera villain, Mackie Messer.
annotation.definitionFit: A translation: in Brecht and Weill's Threepenny Opera the criminal Macheath is Mackie Messer, sung in English as Mack the Knife.

entries.clue: Sharp tooth end needs reshaping (2,3,3)

indicatorNotes.needs reshaping: the letters must be formed into a new shape

annotation.surface: A dentist's note: the pointed tip of a tooth has to be filed down.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Sharp' reads as pointed next to tooth; here it is the time sense, as in six o'clock sharp.
annotation.definitionFit: Six o'clock sharp is six o'clock on the dot: exactly on time.

entries.clue: Austrian cake in good condition did you say? (5)

indicatorNotes.did you say?: asks whether you heard it right, pointing to sound

blocks.note: taut = in good condition, like a well-kept ship

annotation.surface: Someone checks whether an Austrian cake has kept well.
annotation.walkthrough: In a British accent the R in torte is silent, so it matches taut.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a torte is a rich layered cake, the Sachertorte of Vienna being the famous one.

entries.clue: Undersea lodge? Sunken (4-3)

blocks.note: the deep is the sea, and a set (or sett) is a badger's lodge
used of eyes set far back in the face

annotation.surface: An underwater lodge has sunk.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the whimsy: a badger's home at the bottom of the sea.
annotation.definitionFit: Deep-set eyes sit far back in the face: sunken.

entries.clue: Business where dope stocks account with yen (6)

indicatorNotes.stocks: a shop stocks goods, holding them inside

blocks.note: dope and gen both mean inside information

annotation.surface: A shady firm that deals in drugs and keeps its books in Japanese money.
annotation.walkthrough: Dope is drugs on the surface and information in the wordplay; 'stocks' is a verb, so the account holds the dope.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: an agency is a business, such as a travel or estate agency.

entries.clue: Second bed delivered without repercussions (4,4)

blocks.note: a cot is a small bed

annotation.surface: A second bed arrives with no fuss.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Delivered' sounds like a courier dropping off the bed; it is the rescue sense, as in deliver us from evil.
annotation.definitionFit: To get off scot-free is to escape with no penalty or consequences.

entries.clue: See 3
Hunter torn apart long time after deed (7)

blocks.note: an aeon is a very long time

annotation.surface: A hunter was torn apart long after some misdeed.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Torn apart' looks like an anagram indicator, but there is no fodder to go with it; it belongs to the definition. 'After' puts the long time second.
annotation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the hunter Actaeon saw Artemis bathing, was turned into a stag and torn apart by his own hounds.

entries.clue: Hero Weasley here and there enters accordingly (7)

indicatorNotes.here and there: picks letters dotted through Weasley, every other one
indicatorNotes.enters: the letters go into the other word the way a person enters a room

annotation.surface: A Harry Potter fan announces that heroic Ron Weasley makes an entrance.
annotation.walkthrough: Weasley suggests Ron or Harry Potter; it is only there for its letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Theseus is the Greek hero who killed the Minotaur.

entries.clue: X Y and Z advancing initially with the other reversed (4)

indicatorNotes.initially: takes the first letter of advancing
indicatorNotes.reversed: the other is turned back to front

blocks.note: a bit of the other is British slang for sex

annotation.surface: A sexual innuendo dressed up as a list of letters, with someone making advances.
annotation.walkthrough: Advancing and the other set up a romantic scene; the definition is the three coordinate axes of a graph.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: X, Y and Z are the three axes of three-dimensional space.

entries.clue: Kindly man with rodent admitted to hospital department (10)

indicatorNotes.admitted to: the rodent is admitted into the department like a patient into a ward

blocks.note: a vole is a small rodent

annotation.surface: A man and his pet rodent are admitted to a hospital ward.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Kindly' could be an adverb of manner; it is the adjective, meaning well-disposed.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: kindly and benevolent both mean well-meaning and generous.

entries.clue: ESP in later years retains old in clandestine work (9)

indicatorNotes.retains: to retain is to keep hold of, so the later years keep old inside them

annotation.surface: Someone's psychic powers hold up in old age while they do undercover work.
annotation.walkthrough: The O slips in right after the first letter of 'in', splitting it.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: espionage is spying, secret work for an intelligence service.

entries.clue: Something twisted from bad girlie in force with earl (8)

indicatorNotes.bad: bad letters are spoiled into a new order

annotation.surface: A scandal sheet: something twisted came of a bad girl forcing herself on an earl.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Something twisted' sounds moral; it is literal, since filigree is made of twisted wire.
annotation.definitionFit: Filigree is delicate ornamental work of twisted gold or silver wire.

entries.clue: You texted to block pitch about stuff in meeting (10)

indicatorNotes.to block: U gets in the way inside FLING

blocks.note: to fling or pitch is to throw

annotation.surface: A text message tries to stop a sales pitch about the contents of a meeting.
annotation.walkthrough: The pitch takes two insertions, one after its first letter and one after its second. 'Meeting' is a verb here, as in meeting a target.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the sense of satisfying: fulfilling or meeting a demand, a target, a condition.

entries.clue: Strange men affect nurses (7)

indicatorNotes.nurses: to nurse is to hold close, so FEIGN holds OR

blocks.note: to affect a manner is to feign it

annotation.surface: Odd men have an effect on nurses.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Nurses' looks like a noun for the medical staff; it is a verb.
annotation.definitionFit: Foreign can mean strange or unfamiliar, as in an idea foreign to her.

entries.clue: Work round with Manx cat? (4)

indicatorNotes.Manx: the Manx cat has no tail, so the last letter of PUSS goes

annotation.surface: A question about making a circuit alongside a tailless cat from the Isle of Man.
annotation.walkthrough: Manx cats have no tail, a favourite crossword way of saying drop the last letter.
annotation.definitionFit: An opus is a work, especially a musical composition.

entries.clue: See 3
Ancient region’s literary collection preserved? (6)

indicatorNotes.preserved: food preserved in a can is inside it

blocks.note: to can food is to preserve it
ana = a collection of sayings or anecdotes

annotation.surface: A historian asks whether an old region's library has survived.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Preserved' does two jobs: it says the collection is canned, and the tin itself supplies the outer letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Canaan was the ancient land between the Jordan and the Mediterranean.

entries.clue: Controversial writer Heather on line (7)

annotation.surface: A contentious author called Heather is online.
annotation.walkthrough: Heather looks like a first name; it is the plant. In an across clue, 'on' puts the heather after the line.
annotation.definitionFit: J.K. Rowling, author of Harry Potter, has drawn controversy for her public views.

entries.clue: Fish in film additionally appearing in Washington (5)

indicatorNotes.appearing in: to appear in something, like an actor in a film, is to be inside it

annotation.surface: A fish in a movie also turns up in Washington.
annotation.walkthrough: The film is A Fish Called Wanda (1988), a British comedy.
annotation.definitionFit: Wanda is the fish, a woman nicknamed so, in the comedy A Fish Called Wanda.

entries.clue: Taste shown in two-by-two framing loo (7)

indicatorNotes.framing: FOUR frames LAV, standing either side of it

blocks.note: lav and loo are both British words for toilet

annotation.surface: An interior designer shows good taste with a loo framed in a two-by-two panel.
annotation.walkthrough: Two-by-two looks like a size or Noah's animals; it is multiplication.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the flavour of food is its taste, and both words also stretch to style or character.

entries.clue: Backward soldier retreated — and not another soldier? (8)

indicatorNotes.retreated: a retreating soldier goes backwards, so GI turns round

annotation.surface: A soldier falls back, and asks whether another soldier did not.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Backward' sits next to 'retreated' as though it were a direction; it is the definition, meaning slow to learn.
annotation.definitionFit: Backward, in an old sense, means unlearned or ignorant.

entries.clue: American fine wearing dress for expedition (6)

indicatorNotes.wearing: A F wears SARI, so the sari goes round it

blocks.note: a sari is an Indian dress
F = fine, as on pencil leads

annotation.surface: An American in a nice dress sets off on a trip.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fine' reads as describing the dress; it is its own abbreviation.
annotation.definitionFit: A safari is an expedition, usually to see wild animals.

entries.clue: A number want sandwiches trimmed (8)

indicatorNotes.sandwiches: NEED encloses A TEN like bread round a filling

annotation.surface: Many people fancy sandwiches with the crusts cut off.
annotation.walkthrough: 'A number' looks like 'several'; it splits into the article and a specific number.
annotation.definitionFit: Trimmed and neatened both mean tidied up.

entries.clue: Cold symptom — a tissue picked up? (6)

blocks.note: what a head cold makes you do
picked up means heard: said out loud, a tissue is atishoo

annotation.surface: Someone with a cold reaches for a tissue.
annotation.walkthrough: The second half reads as grabbing a hanky; heard rather than read, a tissue is atishoo, the sound of a sneeze.
annotation.definitionFit: A double definition: the common symptom of a cold, and the thing whose noise is spelt atishoo.
